quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should NOT:

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route.
Drive to the next exit, leave the freeway, and go back to your correct exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up in the travel lane or on the shoulder. Continue driving to the next exit or crossroad. Other drivers will not expect a vehicle backing up and may crash into you.

questions.question: Which of the following is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A shaded area of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: A shaded area of the road
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze before other parts of the road and thaw out later. On cold, wet days, these spots become icy.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels facing straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels to the right toward the edge of the road. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the road safely.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights:

options.text: Look toward the center of the roadway.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on course. Do not retaliate by keeping your bright lights on.

questions.question: When passing, move back into the right lane when:

options.text: You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.
You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, there is enough space to safely return to the driving lane.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.
Look to the left and right sides to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the left and right sides to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: Look left and right to check for people or vehicles that may cross your path or enter from another direction.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Move into another lane while in an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane while in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes while in an intersection. Before changing lanes, always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, creating danger. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake firmly.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Take your foot off the gas pedal. This creates space between you and the other vehicle without requiring hard braking or swerving.

questions.question: When parking your vehicle on any hill:

options.text: One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
Your front wheels should be parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and leave your vehicle in "park." If there is no curb, turn your front wheels so the vehicle rolls away from the road if the brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn toward it (downhill) or away from it (uphill).

questions.question: You may not park within ____ feet of a fire hydrant.
questions.explanation: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. Park only where it is legal and where other drivers can see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
5 to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
At the posted speed limit for freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: Merge at or near the speed of traffic on the freeway for safe entry.

questions.question: To avoid hydroplaning while driving in rain, you should:

options.text: Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose contact with the road and ride on top of water. Slow down in wet conditions to prevent this from happening.

questions.question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you space or right-of-way, even when you use your turn signal.

questions.question: You should give extra space when following:

options.text: A station wagon.
A driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
A small car.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles towing trailers cannot see you directly behind them. Keep extra distance when following these vehicles. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
0.02 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: For drivers age 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If you encounter a dust storm while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive through it carefully, since dust storms pass quickly.
Slow down, pull off the road completely, turn off your lights, take your foot off the brake, and wait for the storm to pass.
Slow down, pull off the road completely, turn on your lights, and wait for the storm to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, pull off the road completely, turn off your lights, take your foot off the brake, and wait for the storm to pass.
questions.explanation: In a dust storm, slow down and drive completely off the highway. Stay as far right as possible. Turn off your lights, take your foot off the brake, keep your seat belt on, and wait inside your vehicle until the storm passes.

questions.question: You should always travel at:

options.text: The same speed as nearby vehicles.
The speed limit.
A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should match road and weather conditions and never exceed the legal speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, find a gap in traffic, match the traffic speed, signal, and:

options.text: Expect other drivers to let you in since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to be completely clear before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Find a gap, speed up to match traffic, signal, and merge when safe. Watch other traffic carefully. Do not expect drivers to make room for you.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is turning left:

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut across all lanes.
They must stay on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists travel with traffic on the road. Be ready to see a bicyclist in the left lane when they are turning left.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light. If you have not entered the intersection, you should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Slow down and go through carefully.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: At a steady yellow light, stop your vehicle safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. You may turn left onto another one-way street only if:

options.text: You speed up before the turn.
Traffic flows to the right.
Traffic flows to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows to the left.
questions.explanation: You may turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves left, unless a sign forbids it. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves right.

questions.question: You should signal to turn ____ before you begin the turn.

options.text: 20 feet
50 feet
100 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look straight at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance in darkness. Use headlights properly. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights as the glare can blind you.

questions.question: Streets and highways are most slippery:

options.text: When it rains hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after rain starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after rain starts.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 30 minutes of rain because water mixes with oil and other chemicals on the road. Use extra caution on slippery roads.

questions.question: An orange and red triangular sign on a vehicle always means:

options.text: The vehicle has the right-of-way.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Road work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles like farm tractors, maintenance vehicles, and carts display an orange and red triangle on the back.

questions.question: Turning right on a red light is allowed:

options.text: Only where a sign permits it.
Unless a sign prohibits it.
Only on divided roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Unless a sign prohibits it.
questions.explanation: You may turn right on a red light unless a sign forbids it. Always stop completely and check for other vehicles and pedestrians first.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid sudden braking and sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: On a road with a single broken white centerline, you:

options.text: Must stay in your lane.
May cross the centerline to change lanes.
May change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: May cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines show lanes going the same direction. Broken white lines mean you may pass another vehicle when it is safe.
